summary: Intermittent 502/503 surge during autoscaler warmup causing tenant request failures
description: Issue summary: BrightCart reported a sudden increase in 502/503 responses for a portion of their routed requests beginning ~2026-03-10 02:15 UTC. Impact: customer-facing failures for a subset of API calls tied to streaming and short-sequence generation; estimated 22% of requests for the tenant returned 5xx for a 40-minute window. Scope: single dedicated tenant on Dedicated pools in us-east-1. Timeline: initial spike at 02:15 UTC, remediation actions taken (routing rollback) at 03:05 UTC, stabilised by 03:30 UTC. This ticket captures the investigation, short-term mitigation, and follow-up actions.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use BrightCart tenant credentials and send high QPS streaming requests (~120 QPS sustained) targeting gpt-redwood-7b-instr with max_tokens=256.
2) Ensure dedicated pool autoscaler set to disabled-warmup (feature flag 'autoscaler_warmup=false').
3) Observe API gateway 502/503 rates when pool receives sudden burst from idle state.
4) Re-enable autoscaler warmup or reduce burst to see error rate decline.
logs_and_metrics: APIGW traces: https://traces.redwood.ai/trace/7a8b9c (connection pool exhaustion traces)
Kubernetes events: kube-eviction/pod-restarts for serving-runtime pods in pool-ded-42 (3 pods restarted)
investigation_notes: 02:20 Support: Customer reports ~25% of requests failing with 502/503. Confirmed spike on tenant routing path.

02:30 SRE: Observed sudden increase in backend latency + transient OOM-like restarts on a subset of serving-runtime pods. Correlated with cold-to-hot burst after autoscaler had been disabled for warmup.

02:35 SRE hypothesis: With warmup disabled, autoscaler brings up minimal replicas but does not pre-warm KV cache/embedding prefix caches. Rapid burst causes heavy KV-cache thrashing leading to excessive CPU and memory spikes in runtime; API gateway connection pool backs up and returns 502s.

02:40 Eng: Heap snapshots from two restarts show rapid growth in KV-cache entries; runtime logs include 'kv_cache_evict_lag' warnings. Kernel OOM not triggered, but runtime exited due to enforced watchdog (OOM-like behavior triggered by high RSS).
02:48 Support: Adjusted routing so BrightCart traffic bypassed hot path and was spread to alternate pool with warm cache; 5xx rate dropped immediately.
03:05 Ops: Rolled back infra change from PR 1452 (autoscaler warmup flag set to false in dedicated pools) and restarted affected serving-runtime pods with new config. Traffic normalised by 03:30.

Additional evidence: coredump uploaded to s3://redwood-dumps/serving-runtime/pool-ded-42/core-2026-03-10-02-22.tar.gz. Memory/CPU charts show correlation between KV-cache eviction spikes and 5xx rate.

Related PR: serving-runtime PR #1452 introduced an optimization that disables proactive cache population during scale up when 'autoscaler_warmup=false'. Likely regression under heavy burst patterns for large-prefix workloads.

resolution: Short-term: Rerouted affected tenant traffic to a warm pool and rolled back infra change that disabled autoscaler warmup. Restarted serving-runtime pods to clear cache thrash state. Long-term: Engineering to implement a guard that forces cache population during scale-up for large-prefix/streaming workloads and add a canary test for autoscaler_warmup=false scenarios. Added a runbook entry to quickly detect and route around warmup-related 5xx surges. Follow-up ticket created INT-4021 for rollout of automated warmup fallback and load-test coverage. Customer notified and post-incident summary shared.
